title: Most Americans want AI development to slow down or stop entirely, new poll finds
source_used: Quinnipiac University Poll release of 30 Sep 2026 (poll.qu.edu, releaseid 3969, read in full) and The Decoder (fulltext/C14-05.txt, 983 chars)
key_facts: Quinnipiac University's national poll of 1,202 US adults, taken 24 to 27 September 2026 with a margin of error of 3.5 points, was released on 30 September 2026.

On the pace of AI development: 30% say stop developing powerful AI until its safety can be evaluated, 47% say slow down until safety can be evaluated, 14% say keep the current pace and 5% say move faster.
86% support requiring AI developers to meet independent safety standards even if it slows development; 9% oppose.

73% are very or somewhat concerned that future AI systems could threaten human survival; 74% have little or no trust in the leaders of AI companies; 91% say it is important that the US set guardrails for AI.
81% say safety matters more than staying at the forefront of innovation (14% say the reverse); 69% say keeping up with China matters.
72% would oppose an AI data centre in their community (65% in March 2026) and 21% would support one.
The Decoder (5 Oct) reports the pace-of-development results and quotes Quinnipiac's Chetan Jaiswal that the public wants safeguards that do not depend on taking company leaders at their word.
Same poll release as our 1 Oct edition item 129 (same url), which carried the 73%, 91%, 74% and 72% figures.
quote_evidence: According to a Quinnipiac University poll, 47 percent want to reduce the pace, and 30 percent want a full stop until safety has been verified.

A vast majority of Americans (86 percent) support requiring companies that are developing AI systems to meet independent safety standards, even if it slows down AI development, while 9 percent oppose it.
1,202 U.S. adults nationwide were surveyed from September 24th - 27th with a margin of error of +/- 3.5 percentage points, including the design effect.
why_it_matters_hint: A large majority of US adults back slowing or pausing powerful AI until safety is evaluated, and trust in AI company leaders is low.
event_date: Poll fielded 24 to 27 Sep 2026; released 30 Sep 2026; The Decoder article 5 Oct 2026.
notes: Older news re-dated: the poll came out on 30 Sep and ran in our 1 Oct edition as item 129 (73% concerned about a threat to human survival, 91% guardrails, 74% low trust, 72% oppose a local data centre). The Decoder adds nothing beyond the release; the pace-of-development split (47/30/14/5) is the only part not in that 1 Oct summary. Source and url set to the pollster, the first reporter.
